A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Widget2Code work. All 25 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison; retained material can be matched across relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original widget reconstruction experiments, module ablations in Tables 1–2, and qualitative synthetic-data fine-tuning results in Figure S14.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds a human evaluation and quantitative fine-tuning comparisons in Tables S3–S5.

M1.justification: The core Perceptual Agent, WidgetDSL, compiler, retrieval and adaptive rendering procedures are retained. Appendix F.2 adds integration of fine-tuning into the pipeline, including Ours**, which fine-tunes component extraction while keeping the other modules untuned. Synthetic-data fine-tuning itself already appeared in v1.

E1.justification: The widget dataset, synthetic-data domains and four widget-understanding tasks remain unchanged. The human study uses 100 existing test widgets; the smaller-model and fine-tuning experiments extend evaluation within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Tables S4–S5 newly compare the pipeline against direct Qwen-8B fine-tuning and fine-tuned ScreenCoder, alongside smaller Qwen controls. The original comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: 25 participants rank four methods on 100 test widgets for layout, legibility, style and non-hallucination. Tables S4–S5 also introduce quantitative 8B/32B and selective fine-tuning configurations. The original benchmark split and automatic metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds human validation of the proposed metrics and quantitative analyses of synthetic-data fine-tuning, including whether tuning only component extraction is preferable. These address metric validity and training strategy beyond v1's retained module ablation and qualitative fine-tuning examples.

E5.justification: C.4 adds per-widget human–metric ranking-correlation estimation followed by averaging. The correlation coefficient is not identified, and neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. New Table S3 reports best human ranks for the proposed method and metric–human correlations of 0.93, 0.89 and 0.94 for layout, legibility and style. Tables S4–S5 add fine-tuning results, including SSIM 0.709 for Ours** and 0.657 for fine-tuned ScreenCoder. These are newly reported results under additional configurations, not revisions of the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The retrieval and adaptive-rendering equations and Appendix C's metric definitions and derivations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same task, dataset, evaluation-metric, modular-baseline and WidgetFactory contributions. The shortened conclusion and additional appendix evidence do not materially change these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets fine-tuning as distillation and emphasizes the importance of selecting which modules to tune. Appendix F newly identifies fixed template coverage as a limitation for unseen or emerging components and proposes library evolution and visual or metric feedback. The conclusion's suggestion to expand dataset diversity is removed.

D1.justification: The existing prompts, data-processing instructions, retrieval parameters, color-extraction settings and project-access information are retained. Beyond the new experimental configurations, v2 adds no training recipe, hardware, runtime or resource-access details.

R1.justification: v2 adds SSIM/LPIPS references and citations concerning adaptation, distillation and category discovery without substantially changing its research positioning. It also replaces the Seed1.6 reference with a Seed1.5-VL report while retaining the Seed1.6-Thinking evaluated-model label.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits, an updated corresponding-author footnote, a shortened conclusion, a new human-evaluation subsection and a renamed and expanded Appendix F. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables S3–S5 and makes local layout changes, including moving Figure 7 between columns and relocating existing appendix figures. The original tables, diagrams, qualitative examples and prompt figures are retained without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table S3 adds previously absent human validation of the proposed metrics, while Tables S4–S5 extend v1's qualitative fine-tuning examples with quantitative evidence. The explicit template-coverage limitation also improves the discussion. These gains are limited by unspecified training details, an unidentified correlation measure and absent uncertainty estimates; the Seed1.6/Seed1.5 citation mismatch adds a small traceability problem.
